subject.title: [Bug]: The project won't start on Windows and WSL.

question: Should maintainers pursue a narrow tsdown wrapper/dependency fix after Windows/WSL reproduction, or approve a broader rollback away from tsdown for source builds?
rationale: The report is credible and affects a supported setup path, but the proposed tsc rollback changes build-tool direction and cannot be chosen safely without maintainer intent and platform proof.

options.title: Require focused repro, then narrow fix
options.body: Run or request current-main Windows and WSL first/second-build logs, then choose the smallest dependency or wrapper change that fixes the observed stuck phase.

options.title: Approve a tsdown rollback
options.body: Treat the reporter's diagnosis as sufficient and sponsor a broader replacement of the tsdown build path, accepting the larger migration and validation burden.

options.title: Wait for more reporter data
options.body: Keep the issue open with a needs-info state until full logs identify the dependency, wrapper, or local-state trigger.

recommendation.title: Require focused repro, then narrow fix
recommendation.body: Run or request current-main Windows and WSL first/second-build logs, then choose the smallest dependency or wrapper change that fixes the observed stuck phase.
